scope: only the restored concepts (new numbers 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 11); the rest passed two rounds

concepts.why: Every passage says the Creator in so many words and every note is an exact Berean quotation. The name is a plain label; no tradition is taken a side.

Secular/Jewish reader and the original-arbitrates rule: the Berean's 'In the beginning' in Ps 102:25 renders the Hebrew lephanim ('of old', 'formerly'); the Hebrew has no word 'beginning' (bereshit) there. The relation rests on one translation's wording and the name is that wording, so the verse goes. Heb 1:10 stays (the Greek kat' archas is 'in the beginning'), Gen 1:1 (bereshit), John 1:1-2 (en arche) and Mark 10:6 (ap' arches ktiseos) also say it in the original. Nothing else objectionable: the concept is the phrase only, and the exclusion of Prov 8:22-26 and Ps 90:2 is right.

Biblical-theological and secular readers: (a) Prov 8:27-29 as cut never names wisdom (the speaker, Wisdom, is named only in verses outside the cut) and says 'I was there when He established', i.e. presence, not that He founded the earth BY wisdom; standing alone it does not hold the concept, and its note shows nothing of wisdom. It stays in concepts 6 and 7 where its words (foundations, boundary) are what it says. (b) Ps 136:5 says the heavens were made by 'insight' (understanding), not the earth by wisdom, so it says less/other than the name; Prov 3:19 and Jer 10:12 themselves keep wisdom (earth) and understanding (heavens) distinct. What remains (Ps 104:24; Prov 3:19-20; Jer 10:12; Jer 51:15) each names wisdom with the making of the earth or all things. Jer 10:12 and 51:15 are the same sentence; keeping both is fine as two occurrences.
All eight passages say 'stretched out/stretches out the heavens' and every note is exact. No tradition-dependent grouping; the Old Testament passages are not set beside the New.
Each passage says the earth was founded or its foundations laid; notes are exact. Overlap with Prov 8:29 in concepts 6 and 7 is welcome.

The name is Jer 33:25's words; Jer 31:35-36, Gen 8:22, Ps 74:16-17, Ps 104:19 and Ps 136:7-9 each state the settled course of day, night, seasons, sun and moon; Gen 1:14-18 sets the lights over day and night and the seasons. Notes exact. No side is taken on the days of Genesis (no day is named) or on Israel and the church (Jer 31:36 is quoted as written).

Every passage says dust, formation from it or return to it; notes exact. The name is Gen 3:19's words and the grouping asserts nothing about whether mortality precedes or follows the Fall (Gen 2:7, Ps 103:14, Ps 104:29, Eccl 3:20 are listed as written; the curse is its own secondary concept, with the link to Sin/Exile/Death), so Reformed, Catholic, Orthodox and academic readers can all accept it.
